# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secuura/Blockchain agent | **s140e (SEAT B) — session 2026-09-06 22:24→23:57 AEST** (develop `60d1ce97e` → **`306d0db92`**; TWO merges, both with the tree predicted by `merge-tree` BEFORE the merge and delivered byte-identical and the base held — #871 `e57bd5ac2` tree `a234beabb`, #877 `306d0db92` tree `183207bf7`; TWO PRs built (#875, #878); **TEN tickets filed** (KS-938–944, 946, 947) and two closed as already-fixed with evidence; nothing deployed) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **It took a caveat to a P1 confirmed on a real booted gateway inside one round, and corrected itself twice on the way — once downward.** KS-946: `/api/auth//login` returns **200** with auth receiving canonical `POST /api/auth/login` while the exhausted canonical spelling returns **429** — unauthenticated, any number of slashes, real `index.ts` under `tsx` on its own ports, reproduced on a SECOND independent boot. **It ran the control that could have destroyed its own finding** (three unserved routes → 404, nothing forwarded) and reported it unasked; the control then **CHANGED THE FINDING'S SHAPE** — `/api/nosuch//thing` does nothing, so it is a prefix-strip INTERACTION and not a magic character, which rules out the obvious platform-wide fix. **It put that constraint in the ticket's DESCRIPTION rather than only a comment** — *"the description is where a remedy author will look and it was not there"* — under a heading `WHAT THE REMEDY MUST NOT BE`. **The downward correction is the harder one and it did it while holding the P1 that benefited from the blur:** on the real gateway the MFA bypass does NOT reach the upstream unauthenticated, because its reproduction had omitted `authenticateToken(true)` at `proxy.ts:327`. Its diagnosis is now a fleet standing line: **"I left out the middleware that would have said no"** — a harness built from the MOUNT LIST is systematically more permissive than the product. **It refused to author a remedy** (a normaliser in front of a security gate is where path-confusion bugs live) and refused to claim six of eight mounts, marking them INFERRED. Earlier the same session it caught its own `head -8` over eleven `vi.mock` calls, produced the three-ways-a-search-lies taxonomy, and found `EMPTY OUTPUT IS NOT A RESULT`. Hygiene: processes killed by port and ports confirmed released, 33 containers before and after both boots, probes quarantined by MOVE, `2_Project_Files` ended exactly as found, no hook bypassed, no force push, nothing to Peter or Stuart — **and it noticed a concurrent writer had grown the daily note 1389 → 1621 lines and appended positionally rather than clobbering.** |

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."
